purpose: Assess a publicly retrievable SEAFDEC project update for source-attributed Cagayan River fish evidence and explain how its historical ludong identification relates to later molecular evidence without reconciling separate specimens.

source.title: Attempts to manage Ludong Fisheries in the Philippines
source.publication: Fish for the People, Volume 5, Number 2, pages 36–39
source.citation: Agasen, E. V., Alba, E. B., & Romero, R. O. (2007). Attempts to manage Ludong Fisheries in the Philippines. Fish for the People, 5(2), 36–39. Southeast Asian Fisheries Development Center.
source.license: No item-specific open license or article reuse terms were identified in the repository record or reviewed PDF.

reviewedEvidence.projectContext: The article describes NFRDI's Ludong Fisheries Development Program and says an NFRDI baseline study began in 2006. It reports that morphology-based assessment had difficulty distinguishing Cestraeus taxa but attributed Cagayan River ludong to C. plicatilis. It also says NFRDI DNA profiling was still ongoing at the time of publication.
reviewedEvidence.fisheryAndGear: The article describes gill nets and experimental fish-pot work in Cagayan River and refers broadly to Cagayan and Isabela province areas. It is a project update about fishery and gear methods, not a standardized fish-community survey.
reviewedEvidence.laterTaxonomyContext: A later NFRDI-published molecular study already in the source registry reports 25 sampled ludong from Cagayan and Abra rivers as Cestraeus goldiei. That later identification does not re-identify or supply accession links for the 2006 samples discussed in the 2007 article.

qualityAndReuseLimits: The 2007 article supplies no voucher or museum catalog numbers, sequence accessions, sample dates, exact collection stations, coordinates, or specimen-level rows for its C. plicatilis statement.
The article identifies project objectives and preliminary study context, not a complete Cagayan or Region II fish list.
The historical C. plicatilis label is not substituted for the later C. goldiei identification. The papers refer to separate study samples and are not a verified specimen crosswalk.
The article's historical conservation status, market-price, and gear descriptions are not current taxonomy, abundance, catchability, safety, or legal fishing advice.
No item-specific open reuse permission was found. The SEAFDEC repository's public download access is not treated as permission to reuse article text, photographs, drawings, or tables.
No species/occurrence rows, current distribution claim, geometry, or app data were added.

relationshipToOtherSources.nfrdiMolecularLudongStudy: The later NFRDI molecular study reports 25 sampled ludong from Cagayan and Abra as C. goldiei. It is a separate study and does not provide a voucher/accession crosswalk back to the samples discussed in the 2007 project update.
relationshipToOtherSources.jica2002LowerCagayanAnnex: The JICA Annex V report separately uses the historic C. plicatilis label in its Cagayan basin discussion; it is not a specimen-level confirmation of the NFRDI samples in this article.
relationshipToOtherSources.cagayanAbulog1990Report: This article does not establish that it is the underlying 1990 Assessment and Biology of Fisheries Researches in Cagayan River and Abulog River cited by JICA Table 2.1.3. That report remains unlocated.

nextAction: Keep this source as historical Cagayan project context. Continue retrieving independent Region II freshwater studies with source-linked species rows, exact sites, dated sampling, specimen/accession evidence, and explicit reuse terms; do not publish a broad ludong name or range until the available specimens' taxonomic concepts are reconciled by an evidence-backed policy.
